rules: No built-in strings. No file under packages/*/src may contain a natural-language string that can reach the DOM: text nodes, aria-label, aria-roledescription, aria-valuetext, aria-description, title, placeholder, alt, live-region text, setCustomValidity messages, option labels, link text or text templates. Every such string is supplied by the application.

No language registry and no translations. No adapter or core function reads lang, the document language or navigator.language, and none selects a string, a default or a behaviour from a locale. The vanilla helpers localeOf() and translated() are removed, and so are the core registries getCalendarLabels, fileUploadLabels and getSiteVerificationLabels (see the transition rule below).

Direction is read from dir (core getDirection: computed direction, then the closest [dir]) and never from lang or a locale. A component renders a dir attribute only when the application supplies one; no component defaults to rtl or ltr.

Locale is only a formatting argument: a BCP 47 tag handed to Intl through core formatNumber, formatDate, formatCalendarDate, getCalendarMonth and sortRows. Existing `locale` inputs keep their name. Where the component prints words that Intl generates (Calendar and DatePicker: month names, weekday names, era, formatted dates) `locale` is required in every adapter and core has no default for it. Where it only affects digit grouping or collation (Pagination, RangeSlider, DataTable) it stays optional with today's default. In vanilla the locale comes from options.locale or data-hw-locale on the root, never from an ancestor lang attribute. Formatting adds no words: the Hijri era in month headings now comes from Intl's own era field.

Children before props. The primary visible content of a component (button and link text, alert and dialog bodies, panel and card content, option and item labels in data arrays) is passed as children (React), the default or a named slot (Vue), projected content (Angular) or authored markup (vanilla), and is never defaulted. Text that the component places itself on elements it creates (accessible names, labels of internal controls, headings it renders, live-region and validation messages, templated text) is a named input.

One name per text. A named input has the same name and shape as a React prop, a Vue prop, an Angular @Input and a vanilla controller option. String inputs are named <thing>Label (names and visible labels), <thing>Message (live-region, status and validation text) or keep an established name (label, title, placeholder). Function inputs are named get<Thing>Label / get<Thing>Message and keep one signature in every adapter; they return the complete string and the adapter adds nothing to it.

Vanilla sources, in order: (1) authored markup: the text or aria-label already on the element the controller would otherwise name is used as written; (2) an attribute on the controller root, data-hw-<kebab-name> for string inputs (overflowLabel -> data-hw-overflow-label) and, for function inputs, a template attribute named after the input without "get" whose {placeholders} are filled with core formatTextTemplate (getPageLabel -> data-hw-page-label="… {page}"); (3) the controller option of the same name, which wins over the attribute. enhance() therefore works from markup alone.

Root names. `label` on a component means the accessible name of its root. An aria-label or aria-labelledby that the application passes to the root satisfies the requirement in adapters that forward attributes; a component never invents a name when both are absent.

Required always versus required when. "always" means the text is needed in every use. "when <condition>" is used only for a static switch (a prop, slot, handler or attribute that turns the feature on). Text whose need depends on runtime data (an empty list, overflow, a gap, a failed validation, an unread item) is required always, so a missing string is found at build time rather than in production. "when wanted" marks optional text with no default: when omitted, nothing is rendered for it and no warning is given.

Enforcement in types. React: "always" texts are required props; "when" texts are required through a union on the switching prop where the switch is a prop, otherwise optional. Angular: "always" texts are @Input({ required: true }); "when" texts are optional inputs. Vue: "always" texts are props with required: true; "when" texts are optional props with no default. No prop, input or option may carry a natural-language default, including function-valued ones.

Enforcement at run time. Every adapter calls core requireText(component, name, value, when?) for each "always" text and for each "when" text whose condition holds, at the point where the text would be rendered. Vue and vanilla always call it; React and Angular call it too, for JavaScript callers and for conditional texts the types cannot express. Angular calls it only when ngDevMode is not false. requireText warns once per component and input in development and does nothing in production builds.

Missing text renders nothing. When required text is missing or empty the component renders nothing in its place: no text node, and the attribute is omitted rather than rendered empty. It does not invent a name, reuse another input as a fallback, read the document, or hide the control; structure and behaviour stay the same, and the development warning is the only signal.

Validation never depends on text. A constraint that sets a custom validity message (requiredMessage, invalidMessage, unsupportedMessage, unavailableMessage) still blocks submission when its message is missing: the adapter keeps the control invalid (a single-space custom validity and aria-invalid="true") and warns in development.

No composed sentences. An adapter does not join texts with words or with language-specific punctuation (for example the Arabic comma), and does not prefix or suffix application text with fixed tokens. Where the accessible name depends on data, a function input receives the data and returns the whole string. Glyphs and separators that carry no language (★, ×, /, –, chevron icons) may stay as decoration and are aria-hidden wherever they are not the content itself. Numbers, ISO dates and Intl output are data, not strings.
Developer diagnostics are not user-visible strings: thrown Error messages and console warnings stay in English with the "Hawiyah:" prefix and must never be written to the DOM.

Core API changes that adapters must follow: getCalendarLabels, fileUploadLabels and getSiteVerificationLabels no longer provide text; FileUploadLabels gains getProgressLabel(name) and getRemoveLabel(name); SiteVerificationOptions requires all SiteVerificationLabels and loses locale; getCalendarMonth and formatCalendarDate require locale; new exports hasText, requireText, resetTextWarnings, formatTextTemplate, getFragmentHref, getFragmentId and bindFragmentLink.

Transition. So that adapter builds made before this change still load, core keeps the three registry names exported from packages/core/src/removed.ts with no text in them (every value is an empty string) and typed RemovedExport, which is not callable and not assignable to a label shape: adapter source that still imports them fails to type-check. No adapter may import getCalendarLabels, fileUploadLabels, getSiteVerificationLabels or RemovedExport after this milestone; packages/core/src/removed.ts and its exports are deleted once all four adapters are migrated.
Components that are not listed under "components" contain no built-in strings today (their text is already children, slots, projected content, data or required inputs) and must not gain any.

Open point for the owner: core formatNumber, formatDate and sortRows keep their "ar-SA" formatting default (Latin digits, no words in component use). Removing that default is a separate decision and is not part of this specification.

helpers.name: requireText
helpers.signature: requireText(component: string, name: string, value: unknown, when?: string): boolean
helpers.behaviour: Returns hasText(value). When the text is missing it warns once per component+name through console.warn in development ("Hawiyah: <component> requires \"<name>\"[ when <when>]. …") and returns false; it never substitutes a string. Development means process.env.NODE_ENV is not "production" (bundlers replace it statically; a missing process counts as development); globalThis.__HAWIYAH_DEV__ = true|false overrides the check for pages without a bundler. No browser global is read, nothing runs at module evaluation, and it works during server rendering and without a console.

helpers.name: hasText
helpers.behaviour: True for a string with a non-space character, a finite number, a function (templated text), a non-empty array with usable text and any other rendered value (element, VNode, TemplateRef). False for null, undefined, booleans, empty or whitespace-only strings, NaN and empty arrays. Adapters use it to decide whether to render the element or attribute.

helpers.name: resetTextWarnings
helpers.behaviour: Clears the once-per-input memory of requireText. For tests.

helpers.name: formatTextTemplate
helpers.signature: formatTextTemplate(template: string, values: Readonly<Record<string, string | number>>): string
helpers.behaviour: Replaces {name} placeholders in an application-supplied template with the given values and leaves unknown placeholders as written. Used by the vanilla adapter to turn template attributes (data-hw-page-label="Page {page}") into the same function-valued texts the frameworks receive. It adds no words.

helpers.name: getFragmentHref
helpers.signature: getFragmentHref(id: string, documentUrl?: string | null, baseUrl?: string | null): string
helpers.behaviour: Pure. Returns "#" + encodeURIComponent(id) when no document URL is known (server rendering) or when the base URL equals the document URL without its fragment. When the base differs and has the same origin it returns the document path + query + fragment ("/hawiyah/components/button#main-content"); when the origin differs it returns the absolute document URL + fragment. Reads no globals.

helpers.name: getFragmentId
helpers.behaviour: Returns the decoded fragment of "#id" or "path#id", or "" when there is none. Tolerates malformed escapes.

helpers.name: bindFragmentLink
helpers.signature: bindFragmentLink(link: HTMLAnchorElement, options?: { id?: () => string; navigate?: (id: string, target: HTMLElement) => boolean | void; updateHash?: boolean }): { refresh(): void; activate(): boolean; destroy(): void }
helpers.behaviour: Browser-side binding for one packaged in-page link. It does not touch the href when called. On focus, pointerenter, pointerdown, touchstart, contextmenu, auxclick and click it rewrites the href with getFragmentHref(id, location.href, document.baseURI), so keyboard activation, modified clicks, "open in new tab" and "copy link" all resolve to the current document, including after client-side route changes. On a plain primary click (no modifier, no target other than _self, not already prevented) it finds the target by id in the link's document; if found it prevents the default and either calls options.navigate(id, target) or scrolls the target into view without animation and moves focus to it (adding tabindex="-1" until blur when the target is not focusable). The address bar is left alone unless updateHash is true, in which case history.replaceState writes the resolved URL. When the target is missing or navigate returns false the click is left to the browser. The target id comes from options.id, then data-hw-section, then the href fragment. destroy() removes the listeners and restores "#id" only if the href is still the value it wrote. Returns an inert object on a server DOM (no defaultView); reads globals only through link.ownerDocument.

fragmentLinks.behaviour: Rendered markup: every packaged in-page link is rendered with the bare fragment, href = "#" + encodeURIComponent(id), on the server and on the first client render. That is the only form a server can know, it is identical on both sides of hydration, and it works without JavaScript wherever the page has no <base>. In the browser each adapter binds the link once it is mounted (React: effect; Vue: onMounted; Angular: afterNextRender or an equivalent browser-only hook; vanilla: controller creation) with core bindFragmentLink, and destroys the binding on unmount. Nothing is changed at bind time, so hydration sees the server markup; from the reader's first interaction the href is kept resolving to the current document under any <base href> (same origin: path + query + "#id"; other origin: absolute URL), and it follows client-side route changes because it is recomputed on every interaction. A plain activation (click, Enter) is handled in the page: the default is prevented, the target is scrolled into view and receives focus (tabindex="-1" is added until blur when needed). Skip links scroll without animation; ContentNavigation passes navigate so its observer keeps its existing offset, reduced-motion handling and aria-current update. The URL fragment is not written by default, so hash-routed applications are unaffected; ContentNavigation gains an updateHash option (prop, input, data-hw-update-hash / option) that writes the resolved URL with history.replaceState. Modified clicks, middle clicks, the context menu and target="_blank" are left to the browser with the corrected href. If the target does not exist the click is not intercepted. Adapters must not compute the href during server rendering, must not read location or document outside the mount hook, and must not render an absolute or path-qualified href in server output. An adapter that already handles the click itself (ContentNavigation) may keep its handler and use getFragmentHref for the href on the same events, provided the result matches bindFragmentLink. A skip link is rendered only when its target id is known (AppShell and PortalLayout always have one; PortalHeader only when mainId is supplied). Vanilla: createContentNavigation binds every link it owns; skip links in authored markup (a.hw-skip-link, including those inside [data-hw="portal-header"]) are bound by a new createSkipLink(link) controller that is also registered with enhance() for [data-hw="skip-link"].
